title: varequal
text: varequal R package provides unified interface several classical, robust, rank-based, variance-outlier-oriented procedures assessing homogeneity variances (homoscedasticity), , whether variances response variable equal across independent groups. package also provides high-level functions automatically combining several tests single variance-homogeneity decision. main functionality: *_test Individual tests homogeneity--variance procedure; check_var_equal() wrapper selecting individual test; is_var_equal() higher-level assessment combining five tests.

title: varequal
text: Install released version CRAN: install development version GitHub: load package:
code: install.packages("varequal") if (!require("pak")) install.packages("pak") pak::pak("P10911004-NPUST/varequal") library(varequal)  # For reproducibility set.seed(123)

title: varequal
text: Homogeneity variance important assumption many classical statistical procedures, including one-way ANOVA related linear-model analyses. group variances differ substantially, validity procedures rely common variance can affected. currently implemented individual tests : procedures package test null hypothesis variances across groups equal: \[ H_0:\sigma_1^2 = \sigma_2^2 = \cdots = \sigma_k^2 \] alternative least one group variance differs: \[ H_1:\text{}\sigma_i^2\text{ equal}. \] interpretation follows usual hypothesis-testing framework. small p-value provides evidence homogeneity variance. large p-value means test detect sufficient evidence unequal variances. large p-value prove population variances exactly equal. result interpreted together : sample size group; presence absence outliers; distributional shape response; balance experimental design; scientific magnitude variance differences; assumptions downstream analysis. Different tests different sensitivities. particular, Bartlett’s test can sensitive non-normality, whereas robust rank-based procedures generally less affected departures normality.

title: varequal
text: Ansari_Bradley_test() rank-based procedure assessing equality dispersion. implementation uses approximate chi-square statistic. package documentation notes results may inaccurate small total sample sizes many tied values. test useful nonparametric comparison dispersion, automatically treated interchangeable robust ANOVA-based homogeneity test.
code: ab <- Ansari_Bradley_test(df1, ro ~ grp) #>  #> --------------------------------------------- #>  Ansari-Bradley homogeneity of variance test #>  #>  Response: ro #>  #>  Chi-Square: 6.0855 #>  Chi-Square critical: 7.8147 #>  p-value: 0.10752 #>  #>  #> Group variances are equal.  #> ---------------------------------------------

title: varequal
text: Bartlett_test() implements classical Bartlett test. Bartlett’s test powerful test outliers exist observations follow normal distribution, sensitive departures normality outliers. data satisfy normality assumption reasonably well free important outliers, Bartlett’s test appropriate classical procedure.
code: bl <- Bartlett_test(df1, ro ~ grp, summary = TRUE) #>  #> ---------------------------------------- #>  Bartlett's homogeneity of variance test #>  #>  Response: y #>  #>  Chi-Square: 18.4724 #>  p-value: 0.00035 #>  #>  #> Group variances are unequal.  #> ----------------------------------------

title: varequal
text: Brown_Forsythe_test() provides original Brown–Forsythe procedure Mehrotra-modified version. default method "MBF": original Brown–Forsythe procedure can selected method = "BF": Brown–Forsythe approach robust modification Levene’s procedure uses robust location measure, conventionally group median. package also permits custom transformation response. default based absolute deviations group median: \[ y'_{ij} = |y_{ij} - \tilde y_i|. \] example: method argument distinguishes two implementations: "BF": original Brown–Forsythe procedure; "MBF": Mehrotra modification, adjusts degrees freedom. modified procedure designed reduce Type error inflation, potential trade-power.
code: mbf <- Brown_Forsythe_test(df1, ro ~ grp) #>  #> -------------------------------------------- #> Brown-Forsythe homogeneity of variance test #>  #> Response: ro #>  #>              DF   SS   MS Fvalue  pvalue #> Group      1.96 0.01 0.01 3.9769 0.02918 #> Residuals 32.86 0.05    0                #> Total     34.81 0.06                     #>  #> #> Group variances are unequal. #> -------------------------------------------- bf <- Brown_Forsythe_test(df1, ro ~ grp, method = "BF") #>  #> -------------------------------------------- #> Brown-Forsythe homogeneity of variance test #>  #> Response: ro #>  #>              DF   SS   MS Fvalue  pvalue #> Group         3 0.02 0.01 3.9769 0.01598 #> Residuals 32.86 0.05    0                #> Total     35.86 0.07                     #>  #> #> Group variances are unequal. #> -------------------------------------------- Brown_Forsythe_test(df1, ro ~ grp, transform = function(x) abs(x - mean(x))) #>  #> -------------------------------------------- #> Brown-Forsythe homogeneity of variance test #>  #> Response: ro #>  #>              DF   SS   MS Fvalue  pvalue #> Group      1.89 0.01 0.01 5.0469 0.01406 #> Residuals 30.46 0.04    0                #> Total     32.35 0.05                     #>  #> #> Group variances are unequal. #> --------------------------------------------

title: varequal
text: Fligner_Killeen_test() rank-based procedure particularly useful robustness non-normality outliers important. procedure works ranks absolute deviations group median uses normal-score transformation. Fligner--Killeen important general-purpose choice normality assumption questionable.
code: fk <- Fligner_Killeen_test(df1, ro ~ grp) #>  #> --------------------------------------------- #>  Fligner-Killeen homogeneity of variance test #>  #>  Response: ro #>  #>  Chi-Square: 7.1665 #>  Chi-Square critical: 7.8147 #>  p-value: 0.06678 #>  #>  #> Group variances are equal.  #> ---------------------------------------------

title: varequal
text: Lam_G_test() implements ’t Lam’s G procedure. procedure related Cochran-type variance-outlier assessment rather conventional homogeneity test sense Levene’s Bartlett’s test. supports three alternatives: interpretation directional: "greater" focuses unusually large variances; "less" focuses unusually small variances; "two.sided" considers directions. method highly sensitive outliers, used explicit understanding property.
code: lg <- Lam_G_test(df1, ro ~ grp) #>  #> --------------------------------------------- #> 't Lam's G homogeneity of variance test #>  #> Response: ro #>  #> Outlying group: C #>  #> F-value: 8.3514 #> F-critical: 3.4001 #> p-value: 1e-05 #>  #> #> Group variances are unequal. #> --------------------------------------------- Lam_G_test(df1, ro ~ grp, alternative = "two.sided") #>  #> --------------------------------------------- #> 't Lam's G homogeneity of variance test #>  #> Response: ro #>  #> Outlying group: C #>  #> F-value: 8.3514 #> F-critical: 3.4001 #> p-value: 1e-05 #>  #> #> Group variances are unequal. #> --------------------------------------------- Lam_G_test(df1, ro ~ grp, alternative = "greater") #>  #> --------------------------------------------- #> 't Lam's G homogeneity of variance test #>  #> Response: ro #>  #> Outlying group:  #>  #> F-value: 2.5435 #> F-critical: 2.6257 #> p-value: 0.06043 #>  #> #> Group variances are equal. #> --------------------------------------------- Lam_G_test(df1, ro ~ grp, alternative = "less") #>  #> --------------------------------------------- #> 't Lam's G homogeneity of variance test #>  #> Response: ro #>  #> Outlying group: C #>  #> F-value: 8.3514 #> F-critical: 3.0136 #> p-value: 1e-05 #>  #> #> Group variances are unequal. #> ---------------------------------------------

title: varequal
text: Levene_test() provides ANOVA-based test homogeneity. implementation uses transformation observation measure within-group deviation. default transformation absolute deviation group median: \[ y'_{ij} = |y_{ij} - \tilde y_i|. \] custom transformation can supplied: useful transformations include: transformation subsequently analyzed using ANOVA-style decomposition.
code: lv <- Levene_test(df1, ro ~ grp) #>  #> --------------------------------------- #> Levene's homogeneity of variance test #>  #> Response: ro #>  #>           DF   SS MS Fvalue pvalue #> Group      3 0.01  0 3.1837 0.0325 #> Residuals 46 0.03  0               #> Total     49 0.03                  #>  #> #> Group variances are unequal. #> --------------------------------------- Levene_test(df1, ro ~ grp, transform = function(x) (x - median(x)) ^ 2) #>  #> --------------------------------------- #> Levene's homogeneity of variance test #>  #> Response: ro #>  #>           DF SS MS Fvalue  pvalue #> Group      3  0  0 2.6281 0.06142 #> Residuals 46  0  0                #> Total     49  0                   #>  #> #> Group variances are equal. #> --------------------------------------- # Absolute deviations from the mean Levene_test(df1, ro ~ grp, transform = function(x) abs(x - mean(x))) #>  #> --------------------------------------- #> Levene's homogeneity of variance test #>  #> Response: ro #>  #>           DF   SS MS Fvalue pvalue #> Group      3 0.01  0 4.1116 0.0115 #> Residuals 46 0.02  0               #> Total     49 0.03                  #>  #> #> Group variances are unequal. #> ---------------------------------------  # Square-root absolute deviations Levene_test(df1, ro ~ grp, transform = function(x) sqrt(abs(x - median(x)))) #>  #> --------------------------------------- #> Levene's homogeneity of variance test #>  #> Response: ro #>  #>           DF   SS   MS Fvalue  pvalue #> Group      3 0.04 0.01 2.4066 0.07934 #> Residuals 46 0.28 0.01                #> Total     49 0.32                     #>  #> #> Group variances are equal. #> ---------------------------------------

title: varequal
text: O.Brien_test() implements O’Brien’s variance-homogeneity procedure. default transformation based squared deviations group median: \[ y'_{ij} = (y_{ij} - \tilde y_i)^2. \] O’Brien’s test can conservative may relatively low power forms heteroscedasticity. package documentation therefore places Levene-type Brown–Forsythe procedures ahead O’Brien’s test general homogeneity assessment.
code: ob <- O.Brien_test(df1, ro ~ grp) #>  #> --------------------------------------- #> O'Brien's homogeneity of variance test #>  #> Response: ro #>  #>           DF SS MS Fvalue  pvalue #> Group      3  0  0  2.422 0.07793 #> Residuals 46  0  0                #> Total     49  0                   #>  #> #> Group variances are equal. #> ---------------------------------------

title: varequal
text: O.Neill_Mathews_test() implements weighted least-squares approach Levene’s test. default transformation based absolute deviations group median: \[ y'_{ij} = |y_{ij} - \tilde y_i|. \] procedure useful weighted least-squares formulation desired, particularly group sizes unequal.
code: om <- O.Neill_Mathews_test(df1, ro ~ grp) #>  #> --------------------------------------------- #> O'Neill-Mathews homogeneity of variance test #>  #> Response: ro #>  #>           DF   SS   MS Fvalue  pvalue #> Group      3 0.02 0.01 2.8619 0.04694 #> Residuals 46 0.09    0                #> Total     49  0.1                     #>  #> #> Group variances are unequal. #> ---------------------------------------------

title: varequal
text: check_var_equal() provides common wrapper around individual tests. available method codes : AB: Ansari–Bradley test BL: Bartlett’s test FK: Fligner–Killeen test LG: Lam’s G procedure LV: Levene’s test MBF: Mehrotra–modified Brown–Forsythe test BF: Brown–Forsythe test OB: O’Brien’s test OM: O’Neill–Mathews test particularly useful method selected programmatically. example:
code: method <- "FK" result <- check_var_equal(df1, ro ~ grp, method = method, silent = TRUE) result #> $method #> [1] "Fligner-Killeen homogeneity of variance test" #>  #> $is_var_equal #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $alpha #> [1] 0.05 #>  #> $summary #> [1] NA #>  #> $statistic #> ChiSquare  #>  7.166465  #>  #> $pvalue #> [1] 0.06677704

title: varequal
text: is_var_equal() combines five procedures: Brown–Forsythe; Fligner–Killeen; ’t Lam’s G; Levene; O’Neill–Mathews. sensitivity argument ranges 1 5. larger value requires component tests agree variances equal: Conceptually: sensitivity = 1 permissive; sensitivity = 3 default; sensitivity = 5 conservative. Set summary = TRUE obtain component-test results:
code: for (s in 1:5)  {   cat("sensitivity =", s, "\n")   print(is_var_equal(df1, ro ~ grp, sensitivity = s)) } #> sensitivity = 1  #> [1] TRUE #> sensitivity = 2  #> [1] FALSE #> sensitivity = 3  #> [1] FALSE #> sensitivity = 4  #> [1] FALSE #> sensitivity = 5  #> [1] FALSE result <- is_var_equal(df1, ro ~ grp, summary = TRUE) result$is_var_equal #> [1] FALSE result$summary #>                                  is_var_equal         pval statistic #> Modified Brown-Forsythe (Fvalue)        FALSE 2.918003e-02  3.976918 #> Fligner-Killeen (ChiSquare)              TRUE 6.677704e-02  7.166465 #> 't Lam's G (Fvalue)                     FALSE 1.326224e-05  8.351380 #> Levene's (Fvalue)                       FALSE 3.250316e-02  3.183717 #> O'Neill-Mathews (Fvalue)                FALSE 4.693756e-02  2.861920 #>                                  critical_value #> Modified Brown-Forsythe (Fvalue)       3.310109 #> Fligner-Killeen (ChiSquare)            7.814728 #> 't Lam's G (Fvalue)                    3.400135 #> Levene's (Fvalue)                      2.806845 #> O'Neill-Mathews (Fvalue)               2.806845

title: varequal
text: Different procedures weight distributional features differently. example, dataset can contain: approximately equal variances strong skewness; single extreme observation one group; unequal variances differ primarily one group; several small groups low statistical power; unequal sample sizes. conditions, two valid tests can produce different decisions. Therefore, question simply : test gives significant p-value? better question : variance-homogeneity procedure appropriate distribution, sample size, outlier structure, experimental design? is_var_equal() intended provide practical aggregate assessment, individual functions allow analyst inspect behavior specific procedures.

title: varequal
text: Formal tests replace graphical inspection. example, boxplots can reveal differences spread possible outliers:  graphical strategy can used CYCB1 dataset.
code: text = sprintf("Variance equal: %s", is_var_equal(df1, ro ~ grp)) boxplot(ro ~ grp,          data = df1,          main = text,          horizontal = TRUE,          xlab = "Redox index",          ylab = "Group") points(x = df1$ro,         y = jitter(as.numeric(df1$grp), amount = 0.15)) data("CYCB1") df2 <- CYCB1[[2]] text = sprintf("Variance equal: %s", is_var_equal(df2, cells ~ grp)) boxplot(cells ~ grp,         data = df2,         main = text,         horizontal = TRUE,         xlab = "Cell number",         ylab = "Group") points(x = df2$cells,         y = jitter(as.numeric(df2$grp), amount = 0.15))

title: varequal
text: comparing variance-homogeneity procedures, benchmark uses four possible outcomes: O_O: variances equal method predicts equal; O_X: variances equal method predicts unequal; X_X: variances unequal method predicts unequal; X_O: variances unequal method predicts equal. quantities: \[ \text{Type error} = \frac{O\_X}{O\_O + O\_X}\times100\%, \] Higher value Type error means samples homoscedastic, procedure greater chance mis-classify variances heteroscedastic. \[ \text{Type II error} = \frac{X\_O}{X\_X + X\_O}\times100\%, \] Higher value Type II error means samples heteroscedastic, procedure greater chance mis-classify variances homoscedastic. \[ \text{Accuracy} = \frac{O\_O + X\_X} {O\_O + O\_X + X\_X + X\_O}\times100\%. \] Accuracy represent overall sensitivity specificity samples homoscedasticity.

title: varequal
text: benchmark also considers moderate sample sizes (8 ≤ n ≤ 20) one two outliers. Bartlett ’t Lam’s G can become extremely sensitive introduced outliers, rank-based procedures can maintain substantially better Type II error control. example, reported results include:

title: varequal
text: benchmark supports three general principles: Normal, clean data: Bartlett’s test can highly effective. Non-normal contaminated data: robust procedures Brown–Forsythe Fligner–Killeen preferable. small samples: methods show poor power detect heteroscedasticity (perhaps Lam’s G procedure better choice). benchmark simulation study rather universal ranking methods. Results depend exact simulation design, performance user’s data-generating process can differ.

title: Homogeneity of variance test — check_var_equal
text: method argument specifies statistical procedure used assess whether group variances equal. Available methods : "AB": Ansari-Bradley test rank-based nonparametric test homogeneity scale (dispersion) across groups. often used alternative F-test data non-normal. However, Fligner–Killeen test generally robust recommended purpose. "BL": Bartlett test classical parametric test assessing homoscedasticity across multiple groups. highly sensitive outliers deviations normality. data normally distributed free outliers, robust powerful tests equality variances. "FK": Fligner–Killeen test rank-based nonparametric test homogeneity variances across groups. based absolute deviations median highly robust non-normality outliers. "LG": 't Lam's G test extension Cochran's C test used evaluate internal consistency variances. Although primarily designed variance outlier detection method rather formal test homoscedasticity (Levene's Bartlett's test), can used informally assess variance homogeneity across groups. robustness particularly strong normality absence outliers. "LV": Levene's test classical test equality variances based ANOVA framework. implementation uses median center (instead mean), making robust non-normality outliers. "MBF": Brown–Forsythe test (modified Mehrotra) robust modification Levene's test proposed Brown Forsythe. degrees freedom adjusted following Mehrotra's correction, improving performance non-normality presence outliers. "OB": O'Brien test variance homogeneity test similar spirit Levene's test, based transformed observations designed reduce sensitivity non-normality. "OM": O'Neill–Mathews test modified Levene-type procedure uses weighted least squares approach. methods, null hypothesis group variances equal.
